slides.heading: Reveal Minesweeper
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Recursion
slides.narration: Let's solve Reveal Minesweeper, a medium recursion problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Clicking a mine sets it to "X"; clicking a hidden cell reveals its adjacent-mine count and, if zero, recursively reveals neighbours.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Board of "M" (mine), "H" (hidden), "0"-"8" (revealed). Clicking a mine sets it to "X"; clicking a hidden cell reveals its adjacent-mine count and, if zero, recursively reveals neighbours.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Clicking a mine ends the game; clicking an empty square reveals neighbours recursively.
slides.narration: Clicking a mine ends the game; clicking an empty square reveals neighbours recursively.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, if a mine, mark X. Second, count adjacent mines. Third, if zero, reveal neighbours recursively. Fourth, otherwise show the count.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of w times h. Space is O of w times h.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Clicking a mine ends the game; clicking an empty square reveals neighbours recursively.
slides.narration: To recap Reveal Minesweeper: Clicking a mine ends the game; clicking an empty square reveals neighbours recursively. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
